paragraphs: §Barnabas, Saul, and the Know-It-All

The church in Antioch had some great prophet-preachers and teachers: Barnabas, Simon (nicknamed Niger), Lucius from Cyrene, Manaen (who'd grown up around Herod the ruler), and Saul. One day, while they were worshiping God — fasting too, as they waited for direction — the Holy Spirit spoke: "Set apart Barnabas and Saul for the work I've called them to do."
So they commissioned them. In that focused circle of fasting and prayer, they laid hands on Barnabas and Saul and sent them off.

Sent out by the Holy Spirit on their new mission, Barnabas and Saul went down to Seleucia and caught a ship to Cyprus. The first thing they did when they landed at Salamis was preach God's Word in the Jewish synagogues. They had John with them to help out.

They traveled the whole length of the island, and at Paphos they ran into a Jewish sorcerer who'd wormed his way into the confidence of the governor, Sergius Paulus — a smart man, not easily fooled by fakes. The sorcerer's name was Bar-Jesus, and he was crooked through and through.

The governor invited Barnabas and Saul in because he wanted to hear God's Word straight from them. But the sorcerer — Elymas is his name in plain Greek — kicked up a fuss, trying to keep the governor from believing. But Saul (also called Paul), full of the Holy Spirit, stared him down and said, "You fraud, you servant of the devil — you're up nights cooking up schemes to cheat people out of God. Well, now you've run into God himself, and your game is over. You're going blind — no sunlight for you for a good long while." Instantly a misty darkness fell over him, and he stumbled around begging people to take his hand and lead him.
When the governor saw what happened, he believed — fired up by what they were teaching about the Master.
§Don't Take This Lightly
From Paphos, Paul and his companions set sail for Perga in Pamphylia. That's where John quit and headed back to Jerusalem. From Perga, the rest of them moved on to Antioch in Pisidia.

On the Sabbath they went to the synagogue and sat down. After the Scripture reading — the Law and the Prophets — the synagogue leaders said to them, "Friends, if you have a word of encouragement for the people, please speak."

Paul stood up, paused, took a deep breath, and said, "Fellow Israelites, and all of you who honor God — listen. God chose our ancestors and made our people great while they were still nobodies down in Egypt. Then he led them out with mighty power. He put up with them for about forty years out in that desolate wilderness. Then he wiped out seven nations in Canaan and gave their land to our people — all of that took about 450 years."

"God gave them judges to lead them, right up to the time of Samuel the prophet. Then the people asked for a king, so God gave them Saul, son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin — and Saul ruled for forty years. Then God removed him and made David king, with this recommendation: 'I've found David, son of Jesse — a man after my own heart. He'll do whatever I tell him.'"

"From David's family line, God brought Israel a Savior — Jesus — exactly as he promised. But first, John got everyone ready for his arrival, preaching that they needed a total life-change. As John was wrapping up his work, he said, 'Do you think I'm the One? I'm not. But the One you've been waiting for all these years is right around the corner, about to show up — and I'm about to step off the stage.'"

"Brothers and sisters, children of Abraham, and all of you who honor God — this message of salvation has been sent straight to you. The people and rulers in Jerusalem didn't recognize who Jesus was, and they condemned him to death. They couldn't find any real charge against him, but they demanded Pilate execute him anyway. They did exactly what the prophets said would happen — without realizing they were following the prophets' script word for word, even though those same prophets are read in their synagogues every single Sabbath."

"After they'd done everything the prophets said would happen, they took him down from the cross and buried him. And then God raised him from the dead. There's no arguing with that — he showed up again and again, in lots of places, to the people who'd known him well during the Galilee years. And those same people are still telling everyone he's alive."

"And we're here today with good news: the promise God made to our ancestors has come true for us, their children! He raised Jesus — exactly like it says in the second Psalm: 'You are my Son! Today I celebrate you!' When God raised him from the dead, it was permanent — no going back to rot and decay. That's why Isaiah said, 'I will give you the holy, sure blessings promised to David.' And the psalmist prayed: 'You will never let your Holy One rot in the grave.'"

"David, of course, finished the work God gave him and has been in his grave — dust and ashes — for a long time now. But the One God raised up — no dust and ashes for him! I want you to know, dear friends, that it's because of this risen Jesus that forgiveness of your sins can be announced to you. Through him, everyone who believes gets everything the Law of Moses could never deliver. Everyone who trusts in this risen Jesus is declared right and whole before God."

"So don't shrug this off. You don't want the prophet's warning to be about you: 'Look, you cynics — look hard and watch your world fall apart. I'm doing something right in front of your eyes that you won't believe, even though it's staring you in the face.'"

When the service ended, Paul and Barnabas were invited to come back and speak again the next Sabbath. As people headed out, a lot of Jews and converts to Judaism stuck with Paul and Barnabas, who talked with them at length, urging them to keep living in God's grace.

The next Sabbath, practically the whole town showed up to hear God's Word. But some of the Jewish leaders, seeing the crowds, burned with jealousy. They argued against everything Paul said and made an ugly scene.

But Paul and Barnabas stood their ground. "God's Word had to be spoken to you Jews first," they said. "But since you want nothing to do with it — you've made it crystal clear you have no appetite for eternal life — the door is now open to the non-Jews. And we're walking through it, following God's orders, doing what he commanded: 'I've made you a light for all nations. You will bring salvation to the ends of the earth!'"

When the non-Jews heard this, they could hardly believe their luck. Everyone who was destined for real life put their trust in God — they honored God's Word by receiving that life. And the message of salvation spread like wildfire through the whole region.

But some of the Jews stirred up the most respected women and the leading men of the city, scaring them that their precious way of life was under threat. Alarmed, they turned against Paul and Barnabas and ran them out of town. Paul and Barnabas just shrugged and moved on to the next town, Iconium — filled with joy and the Holy Spirit.
